decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display is a core cardboard point-of-sale format that fits the firm's established business, and a large firm has the slack to keep a low-cost catalogue item without problemistic search.

The pegboard-back shelf display serves steady retail demand for hanging goods and uses existing cardboard capabilities, so there is no clear shortfall against aspirations that would justify dropping it.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a staple product in the display segment and likely meets aspirations, so it stays in the range.
The eighth-pallet display complements the quarter-pallet range for smaller store placements and costs little to keep in the portfolio.

The wooden pallet lies outside the firm's paper core and is exposed to the 2021–2022 rise in material costs, which makes it the most likely candidate for problemistic search, but slack and its role completing the display offering probably keep it for now.
Demand for physical media products is declining, which raises the risk of a shortfall, but the display is low-cost and can be adapted to other goods, so management likely keeps it for another year.
